speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (a) whether the Ministry will conduct a study on the negative health impact of sustained exposure to second-hand smoke from neighbouring HDB units particularly on children and the elderly; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider issuing official guidelines on such negative health impact to inform future policies on regulating smoking out of windows in HDB flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Nonetheless, MOH has been working closely with the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) and the National Environment Agency (NEA) to address smoking related public health concerns.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: In my view, second-hand smoke is a scourge in our heartlands.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: I note that the last time the Ministry replied on this matter was in 2018 and there was a review done then.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: I do not believe the issue has improved and I was wondering why there are no plans to do so again.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: Both sides of the House actually have raised this issue in the House very recently.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: When I looked into the issue a bit more, we were asking about whether we could do more in our HDB flats, but we had not yet confirmed what threshold would lead to a public health concern, including what a threshold of duration qualifies as prolonged.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: So, could MOH reconsider whether it is then timely to make a clear statement on the threshold of how much second-hand smoke is bad enough, and how long the exposure should be before it is bad enough – so that we can then make good policies in our heartlands?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I do agree that it is an issue that we do want to address meaningfully, because we do still see some smokers in the residential estates and people who are living in the flats still trapped.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I do want to state, though, that in as far as the scientific or the medical opinion on the matter is concerned, we are very clear.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is something we do not want and exposure is bad.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, it is really a function of how we then translate it and operationalise it into protecting our people.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But when we are developing these policies, we also have to work together with other partners, including MSE and NEA.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And so, I think this is something that we probably have to look at collectively.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I note that the next Parliamentary Question is to MSE.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Perhaps you can also explore further what can be done.
